Messages.Author: Bernie Bresnahan
Messages.Body:
Game Balance..

How often we've heard that recently..

Here's some more you can think on to "restore" the Balance.
These are my personal beliefs, and are a bit off of the recent
topic (rulings debacle of 7/7)

- Combat cards shouldn't be stackable within a round (we never
played as if they were able to be).

- First Strike should happen before all other Strikes (in line with
Magic:TG) including Dodge and S:CE.

- When building your crypt, Vampires should be considered
Unique. No duplicates in your Crypt.

- If Political Actions can target a Methuselah across the table,
why shouldn't a (D) bleed be able to? Or Bum's Rush?

- V:TES Aggravated Damage worked fine for the last 2 years,
take the old JYHAD rules off the pedestal and get over it.

- Ban Fame. Period. The only people that will miss it are those
that use it in the worst possible combos. No errata will fix this one.

- Decks Size should be defined as 60 or more cards with 6 card Limit.
Encourages Creativity, and cleans up the rule books definition.

If ya'll want to debate over these thoughts, I really don't care..

They're MY opinions, and have some thought behind them.
Of course, many folks here simply knee-jerk a response without
thinking first. It's about what I've come to expect.

>- Combat cards shouldn't be stackable within a round (we never
> played as if they were able to be).

If you mean DotB, sure; if you mean I can't play two Flashes in a round,
I'll have to disagree. This is far too general to implement, in my
opinion. A few cards need 'no more than one foo may be played in
a round' added to their text, but Drawing out the Beast is the only one that's
close to being a problem, and my personal feeling is that it's not big enough
of a deal to be worth it.

>- First Strike should happen before all other Strikes (in line with
> Magic:TG) including Dodge and S:CE.

Well, now *that* would be a dramatic rules rewrite. Nothing in the 6/23
or 7/7 RTRs has mucked with the fundamentals of the game that severely.
First Strike working this way would not only hose Dodge and SCE (as
Immortal Grapple does currently), but it would also hose *any opposing
strike*, if the First Strike sufficed to induce torpor. Shades of TB.

I think this is a really bad idea.

>- When building your crypt, Vampires should be considered
> Unique. No duplicates in your Crypt.

This (like your 6CL comment below) is imposing Card Limits on the game,
a topic that's seen holy wars come and go. Every time the argument can
be reduced to rational discussion, the No Limits camp comes out ahead.

It's not often people come out and ask for 1CL on the crypt, though.
Would you care to tell the group why you feel multiples in the crypt are bad?

>- If Political Actions can target a Methuselah across the table,
> why shouldn't a (D) bleed be able to? Or Bum's Rush?

Bleeds require specific cardtext to affect a non-prey Methuselah, per
definition of 'bleed'. Bum's Rush *can* affect a cross-table Methuselah.

>- V:TES Aggravated Damage worked fine for the last 2 years,
> take the old JYHAD rules off the pedestal and get over it.

The old Jyhad aggro rules haven't been in effect since the VtES aggro rules
were introduced; the 7/7 aggro rules are distinct from either.

>- Ban Fame. Period. The only people that will miss it are those
> that use it in the worst possible combos. No errata will fix this one.

This is part of the whole ban vs. fix discussion, on which I've yet to make
up my mind.

>- Decks Size should be defined as 60 or more cards with 6 card Limit.
> Encourages Creativity, and cleans up the rule books definition.

Ick. See my comments on your 1CL proposal, above.

>If ya'll want to debate over these thoughts, I really don't care..

Whee.

>They're MY opinions, and have some thought behind them.

As do my comments.

>Of course, many folks here simply knee-jerk a response without
>thinking first. It's about what I've come to expect.

"Bernie Bresnahan" <ber...@mich.com> wrote:
> - If Political Actions can target a Methuselah across the table,
> why shouldn't a (D) bleed be able to? Or Bum's Rush?

Political Actions never target a Methuselah - across the table or
otherwise. The referendum called as a political action might, but
all political actions are undirected actions (VTES rules: 18.3)

(D) Bleed cannot because of the rules.
All bleeds (even cardless) are directed - which is to say "all bleeds
are (D)" - the "(D)" is used to denote a directed action (VTES rules:
18.1) - it doesn't alter the action.

Bum's Rush can (card text).

> Do you really believe that

Aside : this is a very debatable area even outside of game-
development. There is a real argument in literary studies
that fixed poetry (poetry with rhyme/meter schemes) is
'better' than free verse, simply because the structure imposed
on the text forces the poet to look at the work with a greater
intensity-of-thought, since he can no longer fall back on the
conventions of ordinary speech. This argument also goes in
for art issues : is a Jackson Pollock 'drip-painting' more creative
than a Rembrandt, because it has fewer strictures concerning
its composition...

In one sense, the strictures of deck-creation _do_ force the
designer to increase creativity, since no longer can he rely on
the 'optimal' set of cards to use. He has to rely on 'second-rate'
cards with similar effects which may have unfortunate costs/
restrictions absent in the preferred card. The deck is more 'creative'
in that it requires more card-selection forethought, and requires
a greater skill-of-play to get the most mileage out of an inefficient
deck.

A NCL deck, however, is designed for optimal performance, given
the parameters of construction. The creativity in such a deck
is enhancing the _modes of operation_ for the deck by removing
anything which does not carry out the main function of the deck
archetype. A card which produces the right effect will by definition
make the deck work most efficiently. The creativity here comes
from minimizing the weaknesses of an overspecialized machine while
maximizing the effectiveness of the deck.

> I think that if every card had a

Personally, I would go along with a 12CL (or a 6CL if every card had a minor
variation). But this would not be a willing transition. If there are 2
different versions of each card, why should I be limited to only 6 of each.
If I really want Catatonic Fear over Majesty, why do I have to put in Majesty
if I need more S:CE? If I want GtU-type cards, but don't have blood to
spare, why can't I load up on Scouting Missions. The coolest thing about the
subtle variations is that you are given a choice, and your deck-building
skills are challenged. The (relatively) simple choice between Scouting
Mission and GtU, for instance... Do you think you'll have the blood to use
GtU. Do you have enough big vamps to use Scouting Mission's superior, or
should you just go with either Computer Hacking or GtU? If you do want to
use the superior, are there more 3 and 7 capacities or 2 and 6 capacities?
This is so much more interesting than... I need 12 bleed cards. Okay, 6 GtU
and 6 Scouting Mission. Not to mention... what if I want a really oddball
deck. Suppose I want to Catatonic Fear my opponents to death. Well... even
though Majesty and Catatonic Fear are almost the same, Majesty won't fit into
this deck. So, now matter how many subtle variations there are, there are
always going to be strategies that need a lot of a single card and can't use
substitutes.

On top of that... I think card limits are just plain arbitrary. A 4CL (or
less), I can see, although I have other, deeper problems with it, and don't
feel that Jyhad works under 4CL. But once you start getting into 6CL or 8CL
or 12Cl... well, then it just seems silly to place any restriction at all.
One of the greatest tenets of deck-building in CL environments is, put in as
many as possible of the cards you use. Therefore, most Magic decks will have
4 copies of each of their really important cards. Most L5R fate decks
consist of exactly 10 different cards, 3 of each (although this changes a bit
with the new 40 card minimum). With 4CL, at least this tenet is kept intact.
When you get to higher card limits, the tenet no longer applies, and you
simply put in as many as you need of each card (better IMO). Well then...
why force a limit to the number you're allowed to "need." Further... the
game is balanced without CL. CL's have always been put in games to balance
decks. We don't need them. We have balance. As for encouraging
creativity... well, I think I've stated my stance on them a number of times.
More decks are possible under NCL, thus more creativity is possible. Plus,
even if CL did encourage creativity, it's kind of annoying for game rules to
require you to be creative.

Well said. Another example of this (from my recent experience):

I've been taking German for the last six weeks. Yesterday I decided to
listen to Brahms' "A German Requiem", one of my favorite pieces. As I
was following the German text from the liner notes (which rhymed in ABAB
format), I noticed that the English translation was not exact. I'm not
talking about idiomatic considerations, just that the English translator
clearly meant the translation to be able to be sung along with the
music. But sometimes German can say something in one word which takes
English four, and vice verse. My point is that I enjoyed the original
German text better.

How does this relate to the Jyhad situation? Well, the text used by
Brahms was under some restrictions: it had to rhyme and had to sound
good with the music he had composed. The English translator had _more_
restrictions: not only did the text have to follow the music, it had to
be a translation of the German, and so some of the original meaning was
lost, and the text suffered as a result.

So while restrictions can stimulate creativity, _too_ many restrictions

This makes permanent manuvers and pressess far more useful than they should be,
and makes Fortitude far weaker than it should be. It also gives advantage to
disciplines that have similar effects in cards with different titles (like
Flash and Pursuit, for instance). As such, say, Celerity has 2 or 3 cards that
give manuvers at inferior while Obfuscate only has 1. The Obfuscate card
(Behind You!) already has a significant disadvantage (balancing the "Cel is a
combat discipline and Obf isn't" argument), and if you could only use 1 per
round, it would be completely pointless to try and compete with Cel, or
permamnent manuvers, with Obf as your manuvering discipline. The only
situation where the stacking of combat cards ever comes into play is the
process of pressing and manuvering, which would become completely hamstrung by
such a rule, and Fortitude, which would become useless with such a rule.

"- First Strike should happen before all other Strikes (in line with
Magic:TG) including Dodge and S:CE."

Perfectly viable.

Unique. No duplicates in your Crypt."

Very bad idea. Makes weird decks completely unworkable. That stupid Nosferatu
spawning deck I was playing saturday night (or my "Deck that only works if you
get Marty Lechtansi out") at Origins is an Obf/Pre Nosferatu vote deck that
uses 3 Harrods and 3 Amadeos. It is a very stupid deck, but fun to play, and
would be completely unbuildable with this rule. It also makes it impossible to
build decks out of any of the non Camarilla clans (Ravanos, Assamite, any
Sabbat). Multiple vamps in a crypt already has a disadvantage in drawing
multiples is bad.

"- If Political Actions can target a Methuselah across the table,
why shouldn't a (D) bleed be able to? Or Bum's Rush?"

I would say that Bleeding already has a severe advantage over Rush combat in
that Bleeding directly works tward your goal -ousting your prey-where Rushing
does not. Rush combat has a bit of flexiblity in that you can Rush people
across the table if you want to. Granted, it is always highly sketchy to do
anything to someone other than your predator or prey, as it usually makes
someone other than you stronger and no one that is hurting you weaker. The
only situation where you "need" to bleed/rush/vote across the table is when the
table is faced by a highly degenerate deck, and all of the recent rules exist
to put an end to this sort of degeneracy.

Let me give you my opinion on First Strike:

Back in the days of Jyhad, we played with First Strike happening
before Dodge, but not before S:CE.
Now, I still think that it should be played that way.
Why? Well, I have 2 major points:

1.) The logical, stick to the rules, point. A strike done with FS
resolves *before* a strike without FS, that's according to the rules.
(If both minions have FS, strikes would resolve normally.) Dodge is
a strike, I think everbody will concur, and as such is resolved normally.
But, if a minion strikes with first strike, the other minions dodge would
resolve *after* the FS. This representing the the FS is a bit quicker than
the normal strike. If the dodge should resolve at the same time, than the
dodger would have to dodge with FS!
You see, with Jyhad it had been that way, and in V:TES this rule was
changed, so that dodge now takes precedence (sp?) over FS. That's not
consistent. S:CE is a different story: even in Jyhad it beat FS.

2.) There aren't that many FS's in the game. The Assamites have some FS,
but they are seldom used. I don't know, but do many players fear FS?
Not a few stated that *weapons suck* - so if they suck already, why fear
the steal/destroy weapon cards? It makes no difference.
IMHO, FS beating dodge(unless FS-dodge) doesn't have an impact on play-
balance, and it helps the Assamites.
It also adds an interesting touch to combat strategies...

So what do you think? Is this worth a debate or not?
Who would like to see FS working like in Jyhad and who of you
fears the power of FS?

Time to make a stand (and Backstab someone :) )

Not errata. VTES rulebook is clear, as you say:

8.3. Special Combat Effects

Dodge: A "dodge" deals no damage, but it prevents the effect of the
opponent's strike that round, even if the opponent's strike was delivered
with First Strike.
Combat Ends: This effect ends combat immediately before any damage is dealt
or a strike card's effects take place. If the acting minion's strike is
"combat ends", the blocking minion may still use a strike card, but this
strike will have no effect. Note that "combat ends" is not affected by a
dodge and cancels a First Strike.
